title: A Neuron Must Work to Die

scenes.tts: When a young neuron loses its survival signal, does it simply run down? Or does it do something?
scenes.visual: Title card: A Neuron Must Work to Die. Question card below it: run down, or do something?
scenes.narration: When a young neuron loses its survival signal, does it simply run down? Or does it do something?

scenes.tts: Picture three wells of young rat sympathetic neurons. These neurons depend on nerve growth factor, N G F.
scenes.caption: Picture three wells of young rat sympathetic neurons. These neurons depend on nerve growth factor, NGF.
scenes.visual: Three culture wells side by side, each with a few neurons. Label: NGF, nerve growth factor.
scenes.narration: Picture three wells of young rat sympathetic neurons. These neurons depend on nerve growth factor, NGF.

scenes.tts: The first well keeps its N G F. Those neurons live.
scenes.caption: The first well keeps its NGF. Those neurons live.
scenes.visual: Well 1 labelled 'NGF'. Its survival curve stays flat near the top.
scenes.narration: The first well keeps its NGF. Those neurons live.

scenes.tts: The second well loses its N G F. Most of those neurons die within a day or two.
scenes.caption: The second well loses its NGF. Most of those neurons die within a day or two.
scenes.visual: Well 2 labelled 'no NGF'. Its survival curve falls over a time axis marked in days.
scenes.narration: The second well loses its NGF. Most of those neurons die within a day or two.

scenes.tts: The third well loses its N G F too. It also gets a drug that stops protein synthesis.
scenes.caption: The third well loses its NGF too. It also gets a drug that stops protein synthesis.
scenes.visual: Well 3 labelled 'no NGF + protein synthesis blocked'. Its curve is not yet drawn.
scenes.narration: The third well loses its NGF too. It also gets a drug that stops protein synthesis.

scenes.tts: What will that drug do? Will these neurons die sooner, later, or on the same schedule?
scenes.visual: Question card held: sooner, later, or the same? Three dashed guesses over well 3's axis.
scenes.narration: What will that drug do? Will these neurons die sooner, later, or on the same schedule?

scenes.tts: Later. The death is delayed.
scenes.visual: Well 3's curve draws in, falling well after well 2's curve. Label: death delayed.
scenes.narration: Later. The death is delayed.

scenes.tts: In nineteen eighty-eight, Johnson's laboratory reported this result.
scenes.caption: In 1988, Johnson's laboratory reported this result.
scenes.visual: Credit: Martin, Johnson and colleagues, 1988.
scenes.narration: In 1988, Johnson's laboratory reported this result.

scenes.tts: Inhibitors of RNA synthesis, or of protein synthesis, kept deprived neurons alive.
scenes.visual: Two drug icons, 'RNA synthesis blocked' and 'protein synthesis blocked', both over a surviving neuron.
scenes.narration: Inhibitors of RNA synthesis, or of protein synthesis, kept deprived neurons alive.

scenes.tts: Why is that strange? A cell starved of what it needs should simply run down.
scenes.visual: A battery icon draining beside a neuron. Label: the run-down idea.
scenes.narration: Why is that strange? A cell starved of what it needs should simply run down.

scenes.tts: Stopping protein synthesis should, if anything, make it run down faster.
scenes.visual: The run-down prediction for well 3: a curve falling sooner than well 2. Crossed out against the real curve.
scenes.narration: Stopping protein synthesis should, if anything, make it run down faster.

scenes.tts: Instead, the neuron has to make something in order to die.
scenes.visual: The neuron's nucleus lights up; new transcripts leave it. Label: needs new RNA and protein.
scenes.narration: Instead, the neuron has to make something in order to die.

scenes.tts: Its death is something the cell does. It is a program.
scenes.visual: Caption on screen: death is something the cell does.
scenes.narration: Its death is something the cell does. It is a program.

scenes.tts: Pathologists describe two broad ways that cells die. The first is necrosis.
scenes.visual: Split screen. Left panel titled 'necrosis'; right panel empty.
scenes.narration: Pathologists describe two broad ways that cells die. The first is necrosis.

scenes.tts: In necrosis, after trauma or loss of blood supply, the cell swells. Its membranes fail.
scenes.visual: Left: a cell swells and its membrane breaks.
scenes.narration: In necrosis, after trauma or loss of blood supply, the cell swells. Its membranes fail.

scenes.tts: Its contents spill out, and the tissue around it becomes inflamed.
scenes.visual: Left: contents spill; surrounding tissue reddens. Label: inflammation.
scenes.narration: Its contents spill out, and the tissue around it becomes inflamed.

scenes.tts: The second is apoptosis. In apoptosis, the cell shrinks. Its chromatin condenses into dense clumps.
scenes.visual: Right panel titled 'apoptosis': a cell shrinks; its nucleus darkens into dense clumps.
scenes.narration: The second is apoptosis. In apoptosis, the cell shrinks. Its chromatin condenses into dense clumps.

scenes.tts: It breaks into membrane-wrapped pieces, and other cells swallow them.
scenes.visual: Right: the cell buds into wrapped fragments; a neighbouring cell engulfs them.
scenes.narration: It breaks into membrane-wrapped pieces, and other cells swallow them.

scenes.tts: A nucleus condensed this way is called pyknotic.
scenes.visual: Close-up of a small, dark, condensed nucleus. Label: pyknotic nucleus.
scenes.narration: A nucleus condensed this way is called pyknotic.

scenes.tts: Early studies of neuron death in embryos counted these pyknotic nuclei.
scenes.visual: A tissue section of an embryo with dark pyknotic nuclei ticked off one by one.
scenes.narration: Early studies of neuron death in embryos counted these pyknotic nuclei.

scenes.tts: The neuron's program raises three puzzles.
scenes.visual: Three empty numbered boxes appear.
scenes.narration: The neuron's program raises three puzzles.

scenes.tts: First, what must a deprived neuron make, in order to die?
scenes.visual: Box 1 fills: What must be made?
scenes.narration: First, what must a deprived neuron make, in order to die?

scenes.tts: Second, which proteins carry out the death?
scenes.visual: Box 2 fills: What are the parts?
scenes.narration: Second, which proteins carry out the death?

scenes.tts: Third, what keeps those proteins off while N G F is present?
scenes.caption: Third, what keeps those proteins off while NGF is present?
scenes.visual: Box 3 fills: What keeps them off while NGF is present?
scenes.narration: Third, what keeps those proteins off while NGF is present?

scenes.tts: So hold on to one fact. A deprived young sympathetic neuron in culture does not just fade. It runs a program that needs new RNA and protein.
scenes.visual: End card line: a deprived neuron runs a program that needs new gene expression.
scenes.narration: So hold on to one fact. A deprived young sympathetic neuron in culture does not just fade. It runs a program that needs new RNA and protein.
